summary: A 60-foot steel fire tower on a 92-acre Missouri Conservation towersite near St. James; reported standing and listed as climbable in 2019, not checked since.

events.note: A 60-foot steel tower is recorded at the Rosati site. The guide gives no construction date.

Towerman Eugene Farrow, Sr. transferred from the Rosati tower to the Lennox tower; Justein E. McMillen took his place at Rosati.
Bathroom and roof repaired at the towersite (fiscal 1965-66).
Major repairs made to the Rosati tower residence (fiscal 1967-68).
Overhead garage doors hung at the towersite (fiscal 1969-70).
Neosho Daily News item, as quoted by the guide: the department once had a chestnut plantation at the towersite and its foresters collected seed. The planting's date is not given.

notes_for_editor: Standing and climbable status rest on a single October 2019 newspaper report, not a current check; verify with MDC before anyone climbs. The 1941 date is the earliest date in the guide and is not shown to be the build date. The guide's 60-foot figure is kept; an anonymous undergroundozarks forum thread (viewtopic t=7137) recalls a 50 ft tower that is still active and describes a gate, but it was not used as a source. The MDC map gives 92 acres and a gate symbol but does not state whether the public may enter, so no access level is recorded. A survey memo (files.lqdt1.com 11790_15_0.pdf) surfaced in search and appears to describe the Rosati tower's steel frame and footings, but the cached PDF returned no text, so it is not cited; a person could OCR it to check the current condition. Forward: confirm current access and climbing status with MDC.
